html:
The Couture complex is the name archaeologists give to a Middle Woodland culture of the Detroit River and western Lake Erie country, in what is now southwestern Ontario and nearby Michigan and Ohio. On this map it covers about 100 BCE to 500 CE.

Little is known about it beyond its sites and pottery. Like its neighbours, the Saugeen people to the northeast and the Goodall people to the west, its people lived by fishing, hunting and gathering, and were touched by the trade and burial customs of the Hopewell world.
